For general $d$, $p \in \{0, \dots, d\}$.
*   **Smoothing Coefficient ($\alpha$):** Used in vertex repositioning.
The refinement from pass $p$ to $p+1$ involves inserting vertices and merging pyramids.
The process is recursive over passes $0$ to $d$ (or $0$ to $3$ for 3D).
*   For each cell $C_i$ in the current mesh, compute its center $p_i$.
*   Decompose $C_i$ (with $n$ facets) into $n$ pyramidal cells by connecting $p_i$ to each facet $f_k$.
*   For each cell $F_k$ in the pass 1 mesh, determine its center $q_k$.
*   Decompose $F_k$ into pyramids by connecting $q_k$ to new facets $g_i$ generated in pass 1.
*   Each resulting pyramid contains exactly one edge $e_j$ from the pass 0 mesh.
*   Merge all pyramids incident to the same edge $e_j$ into a cell $E_j$.
*   Determine the center $r_i$ of each cell $E_i$.
*   Refine $E_i$ by joining $r_i$ with each facet.
*   Insert a vertex $q$ at the center of a $(d-p)$-dimensional face of the base mesh $M_l$.
*   Partition cell $c$ into pyramids by connecting $q$ to all facets.
*   Merge all pyramids containing a common $(d-p-1)$-dimensional face of $M_l$.
*   Insert vertex $q$ at the edge of $M_l$.
For non-boundary/non-sharp features, $q$ is the center of $c$.
*   Partition $c$ into pyramids by connecting $q$ to facets not containing $q$.
*   In 3D rectilinear grid refinement: Pass 1 adds 1 vertex per original vertex (doubling total).
Pass 2 adds 3 vertices per original vertex (factor of 2.5 increase).
